articles.title: ‘Clean Hands’ Review: Zach Braff Is a Cop on a Crusade to Save His Addict Daughter in an Uneasy Fact-Based Crime Drama
articles.summary: When a filmmaker tells a story based on real events, especially ones that are inspiring or heroic, there’s always a risk of hagiography. “Clean Hands” is a movie where the storytellers either take a lot of license with an actual person’s life to add drama, or don’t seem aware just how unflattering…
body: Jake Allyn's film tells the story of Kevin Simmers, a real-life narcotics officer whose professional and personal lives clash over his teenage daughter Brooke's heroin addiction.

Despite the support of his religious wife Dana (Abigail Spencer) and colleagues on the police force, including an ambitious deputy (Lucas Till) eager to succeed him as the precinct’s role model, Simmers’ efforts to help get Brooke clean fail over and over again. As he faces the prospect of losing her to addiction, he begins to conceive an alternative path for struggling drug abusers, even while witnessing members of the Hagerstown community — including some of his fellow officers — exploiting addicts instead of helping them.

articles.title: ‘Tommy & Tuppence’ Stars Josh Dylan and Antonia Thomas on That ‘Intense’ Finale, Why the Detective Duo ‘Keep Missing Each Other’ Romantically and a Potential Season 2
articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers for Episode 6 of “Tommy & Tuppence,” now streaming on BritBox. The finale of “Tommy & Tuppence” finds the Agatha Christie detective duo, played by Josh Dylan and Antonia Thomas, on the verge of a new chapter.
body: “Finally, it clicks and she realizes — but is she just a bit too late?” Thomas tells Variety over Zoom.

“Much of their relationship is characterized by sliding doors moments and missing each other just by a hair’s breath, which is in part infuriating but also kind of tantalizing,” Dylan adds. “It’s like, when are they going to get it out?!”
Below, Dylan and Thomas break down the finale episode, reveal how they established Tommy and Tuppence’s chemistry and discuss a potential Season 2.

Dylan: Obviously, Agatha Christie is untouchable in so many ways — incomparable rather, because she’s the Queen of Crime and it’s beloved by people. But when I read the scripts I felt like, here’s an opportunity to do something that I don’t think I’ve seen before, which is blending that cozy crime world, that Agatha Christie world, with an opportunity to make this feel really grounded and naturalistic and real.

articles.title: Why the ‘Girls’ Revival Is Such an Exciting Idea
articles.summary: The return of “Girls” for a five-episode limited run won’t just be interesting because of how Hannah Horvath has or has not changed. It’ll be a litmus test for how we at home have, as well. After all, Lena Dunham has at times struggled to distinguish herself from her most famous creation.
body: In all, though, it was invigorating to see Carrie Bradshaw ripped out of her moment and placed into contemporaneity. And Hannah Horvath has similar promise. Since “Girls” ended, she’s been frozen in time — our reactions to her may have shifted, but she remains a creature of the late Obama era, as emblematic of old-millennial mores and ways of speaking as Carrie Bradshaw was of turn-of-the-century Gen X fabulosity. How has Hannah’s perspective shifted since we left her — and what parts of her remain irreducibly herself? Much in the same way that I’ve loved watching Dunham coming into herself in recent years, I can’t wait to find out.

articles.title: ‘A tipping point of ickiness’: Welsh star Tom Rhys Harries on playing eyelid-snipping DC supervillain Clayface
articles.summary: He cut his teeth playing rock stars and pretty posh boys. Speaking from his LA home, the actor talks about landing his first blockbuster lead in the grisly DC horror. Will it be too shocking for comic book fans?
body: Exactly 13 years ago this month, Tom Rhys Harries was hanging by his ankles from a meat hook every night. Playing a teenage rock’n’roll idol abducted by gangsters in a revival of Jez Butterworth’s Mojo, Harries was fresh out of drama school and the only unknown in a cast led by Ben Whishaw and Rupert Grint. The Guardian’s Michael Billington likened him to “an embryonic Elvis”.

Now the 36-year-old Cardiff-born actor has the title role in Clayface, a violent DC Comics supervillain blockbuster set in Batman’s stomping ground, Gotham City. This puts him in the company of fellow Brits in the comic-book universe, such as Tom Holland (Spider-Man), Robert Pattinson (Batman) and David Jonsson, recently announced as the new Black Panther. “I felt ready to do this,” says Harries. “Had I been younger, I’d have been suffocated by the insecurity of wanting to do a good job but not having that quiet trust in getting there.”

Harries has earned the right to relax. He spent three months auditioning to play the severely mutilated protagonist of Clayface for producers James Gunn (Guardians of the Galaxy) and Matt Reeves (The Batman). How did he stay sane all that time? “I didn’t.”
points: He cut his teeth playing rock stars and pretty posh boys.
Speaking from his LA home, the actor talks about landing his first blockbuster lead in the grisly DC horror.

articles.title: Ex-gang boss sentenced to 40 years for orchestrating Tupac Shakur's murder
articles.summary: Davis was found guilty last month over his role in the late rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in 1996.
body: Former gang boss Duane "Keffe D" Davis has been sentenced to at least 40 years in prison for orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur.

A jury found Davis, 63, guilty in September of one count of murder with a deadly weapon for the rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on 7 September 1996. He has said he will appeal the verdict.

Prosecutors argued that although Davis did not fire the gun himself, he was the ringleader of the group that committed the murder. He admitted in his memoir that he had provided the gun used in the crime.
Davis' conviction was the first in a cold case that has intrigued hip-hop fans for nearly 30 years.
points: Davis was found guilty last month over his role in the late rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in 1996.

articles.title: Forever Is Now review – political study of former Irish Green leader is like The Thick of It but with morals
articles.summary: Eamon Ryan is shown to be principled, likable and hard working in a glowing portrait, filmed while serving in the country’s coalition government. This fly-on-the-wall documentary about the former Irish Green party leader and cabinet minister Eamon Ryan reminded me of the political satire The Thick…
body: The title is something that Ryan’s 25-year-old son Tommy repeats over and over. “Forever … forever … forever.” Tommy is autistic and requires full-time care. When Ryan resigns from government, one of his reasons is to spend more time with Tommy. We see the pair of them at the allotment picking raspberries and walking the dog. But other than a quick glimpse of his wife, Victoria, the rest of Ryan’s family life is kept firmly behind closed doors.

Instead, the cameras trail him on the road, talking to angry residents of an Irish town submerged by flood waters (again), and hustling at the UN general assembly in New York and two Cop conferences. At his side is formidable media adviser Edel Hackett (Malcolm Tucker with morals), who sifts through the daily torrent of online abuse, harassment and intimidation slung Ryan’s way.
points: Eamon Ryan is shown to be principled, likable and hard working in a glowing portrait, filmed while serving in the country’s coalition government.

articles.title: Parke Brings Back Its Sold-Out Shrunken Sweatshirt in Fan-Favorite Colorways
articles.summary: The brand's limited-edition launch reissues the cropped version of its signature (always out-of-stock) mockneck and restocks the beloved original in core shades.
body: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission.

Within two weeks of Parke’s Pink Aid partnership and just one month after its Fall ’26 Collection, the internet-famous label launches the Everyday Edit, welcoming back one of its most viral pieces to date: the Shrunken Varsity Mockneck. The limited-edition clothing capsule, available online on Tuesday, Oct. 13, also includes a restock of Parke’s (perpetually sold-out) original Varsity Mockneck in the brand’s core colorways, along with new iterations of its staple sweatpants and sweatshirts.

The new Raglan Mockneck is another collection standout. Crafted from Parke’s signature fleece, the laid-back, sporty style is a fresh take on the brand’s cult-classic Varsity Mockneck. It’s available in both gray and rose, and retails for $125.

articles.title: Highdee Kuan on ‘Brothers’ and Getting Her Very Own ‘True Detective’ Moment on the Apple Comedy
articles.summary: The actress plays Woody Harrelson's daughter Olive in the family comedy that stars Harrelson and Matthew McConaughey as heightened versions of themselves.
body: Highdee Kuan is excited to finally be able to share her new Apple TV+ show Brothers with the world.

“We started going into production a year ago, so it feels like it’s nice to usher this into the world,” actress says. “We just had such a great time in Austin with the cast and crew, so it just feels like watching it, reliving really special and fun times with everyone.”

In the show’s most recent episode, Kuan’s character Olive goes on a sleuthing quest to help her father clarify if he and McConaughey are indeed brothers — the main question behind Brothers. It’s a turning point for the show, and it’s a turning point for Olive, whose broken engagement kicks off the series. It’s her very own True Detective moment, as her character puts it.
Below, Kuan speaks with THR about playing Harrelson’s daughter, their relationship in show and how she came to join the series.

articles.title: Katie Price denies 'any venom' against ex at his rape trial
articles.summary: Kieran Hayler, who denies offences against a girl when she was 13, was married to Price at the time.
body: Katie Price has denied having "any venom" against her ex-husband at his rape trial.
Kieran Hayler is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one of sexual assault against a then-13-year-old girl in West Sussex in 2016, all of which he denies.
When challenged by defence lawyer Arlette Piercy on her view of her ex-husband, Price said: "I don't have any venom against Kieran, it was amicable when we split."
During her evidence to Lewes Crown Court, Price was asked by Piercy if she "loved revenge or is it just TV?".

articles.title: Pablo Torre Reveals Art of Play Security Camera Footage, and It Doesn’t Look Great for Kelly Clarkson
articles.summary: Clarkson fans are going to want to look away from a moment like this.
body: Pablo Torre promised us security footage from Kelly Clarkson ‘s now-viral visit to Art of Play in Brooklyn. Well, we did get the video on Tuesday night, but no audio — bummer.
The OG American Idol was in the toy store for exactly four minutes, 50 seconds. What we could see of the brief visit does not bode well for the Stronger singer.

On her way out of the store, Clarkson appears to share strong feelings toward a second man, who is working the cash register. She’d share those same strong feelings on social media exactly 15 minutes after her exit.
The “comparable” product was a pair of other automaton birds made by a German clockmaker. It cost $2,000. Torre purchased it, unveiled it on his show, and said he would auction it off.
